title: Pin comment's bite vector is wrong: breaking the re-pricing branch makes the (res,host) route VANISH (count 0), not 'FLIP to m2'
detail: Toggle-verified: disabling the branch gives count 0 (pin line 254 'got 0'), no FLIP — dist[m1] stays 5 via per-pipe relaxation; 5+20=25≠10 and 10+10=20≠10, so NO neighbor satisfies the equality test.
recommended_fix: Reword the bite-vector comment: breaking pass-1 re-pricing leaves min_cost at 20 while dist keeps 5, so the equality test matches no neighbor — the (res,host) route VANISHES (count 0).

title: New pin dereferences hops[off] after the non-fatal count==1 check — mis-reads an unrelated hop row in the bite scenario
evidence:
testing.expectf(t, count == 1,
		"the re-priced fat bundle must win UNIQUELY (count 1), got %d", count)
	testing.expectf(t, s.routing.hops[int(off)].node == m1,
		"next hop must be m1 (bundle priced at its min member: 5+5=10), got %d — the bundle edge was NOT re-priced",
		s.routing.hops[int(off)].node)
detail: expectf records and CONTINUES. Toggle-verified: with the branch broken, count==0 leaves off=0, so lines 256/286 mis-read hops[0] (unrelated slot: 'got 3', 'got 2') and emit misleading 'NOT re-priced' messages. Replicates accepted r1 note #3.
recommended_fix: Guard the node/pipe asserts with `if count == 1` (and the tier/pipe asserts with `if rep_slot != -1`) so a broken branch fails with the pinned message only.
